papers.title: Molecular mimicry and functional convergence of bacterial proteins in host-microbe interactions.
papers.abstract: Bacterial proteins modulate host immunity through diverse molecular strategies that are often broadly described as molecular mimicry. However, inconsistent terminology has obscured distinctions between genuine host-like interactions and other forms of host-directed immune modulation. We propose an operational framework that classifies bacterial proteins into four mechanistic categories: molecular mimicry, mimic-like behavior, functional convergence, and pathway interference. The framework prioritizes explicit criteria, including host-target engagement, interaction-interface similarity, functio
papers.summary: This perspective proposes a clear operational framework for classifying bacterial proteins that modulate host immunity, distinguishing true molecular mimicry from mimic-like behavior, functional convergence, and pathway interference. By prioritizing explicit criteria such as host-target engagement and interaction-interface similarity, it aims to resolve terminological confusion in host-microbe interaction research.

papers.title: Prescribed burns drive lasting changes in soil nitrogen cycling and microbial function.
papers.abstract: Fire is a major pulse disturbance to soil microbial communities, with broad implications for nutrient cycling; however, regular burning is also a natural and often-essential process maintaining biodiversity in unique and imperiled fire-dependent ecosystems. Prescribed fire is widely used to promote this biodiversity and simultaneously reduce wildfire risk. Although such repeated burning is known to alter surface biodiversity, belowground soil geochemistry, and soil microbial community structure, the functional consequences (i.e., the metabolic capabilities that underlie the ecosystem services
papers.summary: This study examines how repeated prescribed burns affect soil microbial communities and nitrogen cycling in fire-dependent ecosystems. The authors find that regular burning causes lasting shifts in soil nitrogen cycling and microbial metabolic functions, even as it supports aboveground biodiversity and reduces wildfire risk. The work highlights a trade-off between conservation burning and belowground ecosystem function.

papers.title: Dental spittoon biofilms as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance: a longitudinal multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Dental chair spittoons are chronically exposed to saliva, aerosols, intermittent water flow, and chemical disinfectants, yet their biofilm ecology and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dynamics remain poorly defined. We applied longitudinal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and culture-based antimicrobial susceptibility testing to biofilms collected across four dental departments at three time points. Community analyses revealed significant temporal succession and department-specific structuring, indicating the establishment of stable, ecologically differentiated biofilm systems. Nu
papers.summary: This longitudinal multi-omics study characterizes biofilms in dental chair spittoons across four departments and three time points, revealing stable, department-specific microbial communities that undergo temporal succession. The work identifies these biofilms as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes and resistant organisms, highlighting an underappreciated environmental AMR source in clinical dental settings.

papers.title: Pathogen-oriented mNGS is not equivalent to microbiome profiling: interpreting BALF mNGS diversity in ARDS.
papers.abstract: Gao et al. provide valuable data-linking bronchoalveolar lavage fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing with inflammatory subphenotypes of acute respiratory distress syndrome. We highlight three issues relevant to interpretation: an apparent inconsistency concerning exclusion of samples with no micro-organisms detected, use of a pathogen-oriented workflow for community-level ecological inference, and the distinction between detection yield and diagnostic performance without an independent reference standard. Clarification of sample eligibility, sensitivity analysis including technically v
papers.summary: This commentary critiques a study that used pathogen-oriented metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) on bronchoalveolar lavage fluid to infer microbial community ecology in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The authors argue that such a workflow is not equivalent to microbiome profiling, and they raise concerns about sample exclusion criteria, ecological inference from a pathogen-focused assay, and the lack of an independent reference standard for assessing diagnostic performance. The letter calls for clarification of sample eligibility and sensitivity analyses.

papers.title: Community-level eDNA decay patterns in marine zooplankton: Implications for optimizing eDNA-based marine environmental monitoring.
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has the potential to greatly transform marine ecological monitoring, yet its capacity for accurate biodiversity estimates is constrained by its decay process. Previous research has largely focused on laboratory-cultured single species, and thus the dynamics of mixed-species eDNA from natural communities remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted a 10-day time-series experiment to track the community-level eDNA decay process following the complete removal of zooplankton, employing an integrated approach of morphological analysis, quantitative PCR (qPCR), metabarcoding
papers.summary: This study tracked how environmental DNA from a natural marine zooplankton community degrades over 10 days after the organisms were removed, using morphology, qPCR, and metabarcoding together. It addresses a gap left by prior single-species laboratory decay studies, showing how mixed-species eDNA decays at the community level. The findings aim to help calibrate eDNA-based biodiversity estimates for marine monitoring.

papers.title: Antimicrobial-resistant organism carriage and metagenomic characterization of the microbiome and resistome in veterinary workers.
papers.abstract: Veterinary personnel work in environments with high exposure to antimicrobials and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. However, the extent to which these occupational exposures influence their carriage of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) organisms and the composition of their microbiome and resistome remains poorly understood. The objective of this study was to characterize AMR pathogen carriage and microbiome/resistome composition in veterinary personnel and to assess whether workplace setting and patient-related exposures were associated with detectable differences in these outcomes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) organism carriage and the composition of the microbiome and resistome in veterinary workers, a group with high occupational exposure to antimicrobials and resistant pathogens. It examines whether workplace setting and patient-related exposures are associated with detectable differences in AMR carriage and microbiome/resistome profiles.

papers.title: Perseus: Lineage-Aware Refinement of Kraken2 Taxonomic Classification for Long Read Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Long-read metagenomic sequencing improves assembly contiguity and enables genome-resolved analysis of complex microbial communities, but accurate taxonomic classification of long reads and assembled contigs remains challenging. Highly scalable k-mer-based classifiers such as Kraken2 frequently over-assign fine-rank taxonomic labels when applied to long-read data, producing high false positive classification rates driven by sparse or localized k-mer matches, particularly in microbiomes with extensive taxonomic novelty.
papers.summary: Perseus is a new method that refines Kraken2 taxonomic classifications for long-read metagenomes by using lineage-aware information to correct over-assignment of fine-rank labels. It addresses the high false positive rates that occur when k-mer-based classifiers are applied to long reads, especially in microbiomes with novel taxa. This improves the accuracy of taxonomic classification for long-read and assembled contig data.

papers.title: Symbiotic interactions and climate change implications of the octocoral microbiome.
papers.abstract: Octocorals are vital components of tropical, temperate, and cold-water benthic marine ecosystems. Their associated microbiomes, comprising microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses, are increasingly recognised as central to host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defence. Metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have uncovered taxonomic and functional complexity within these microbial communities, revealing patterns of host specificity and health status, along with seasonality and geographic structuring. However, anthropogenic stressors, particularly those associated with global climate change
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on octocoral microbiomes, which include microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses that contribute to host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defense. It highlights patterns of host specificity, seasonality, and geographic structuring revealed by metagenomics and amplicon sequencing, while emphasizing how climate change stressors threaten these symbiotic interactions.

papers.title: The canine gut microbiome as a translational model for human health and aging.
papers.abstract: The domestic dog is increasingly recognized as a complementary translational model for microbiome research relevant to human health while also offering direct benefits for veterinary medicine. Dogs share environments and dietary exposures with humans and show substantial taxonomic and gene-content similarity to the human gut microbiome, although the apparent degree of similarity depends strongly on whether read recruitment, gene-catalog overlap, or functional overlap is assessed. Dogs also develop spontaneous chronic enteropathies, obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, cancers, cognitive d
papers.summary: This review argues that the domestic dog is a valuable translational model for studying the gut microbiome's role in human health and aging, given shared environments, diets, and substantial taxonomic and functional similarity between canine and human gut microbiomes. It notes that the apparent degree of similarity depends on the analytical approach used (read recruitment, gene-catalog overlap, or functional overlap), and highlights that dogs naturally develop conditions like chronic enteropathies, obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, cancers, and cognitive decline relevant to human disease.

papers.title: Multi-omics evidence reveals robust airborne-human resistome connectivity driven by high-risk ARGs and mediated by Staphylococcus.
papers.abstract: Airborne microbiomes are considered an important source of human antimicrobial resistance (AMR) exposure, yet multi-omics evidence linking airborne and human nasal resistomes remains limited. Here, we integrated metagenomic sequencing and whole-genome sequencing of antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus isolates to investigate the connectivity between air and human nasal resistomes in dairy farm environments. Metagenomic taxonomic profiling showed that Staphylococcus was prominent in total suspended particles (TSP) and consistently detected across all samples. Among environmental reservoirs, TSP
papers.summary: This study integrates metagenomics and whole-genome sequencing of antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus isolates to show that airborne resistomes in dairy farm environments are strongly connected to human nasal resistomes. Staphylococcus appears to act as a key mediator carrying high-risk antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) between air and humans, suggesting airborne transmission is an important exposure route for AMR.

papers.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Taxonomic profiling is fundamental to microbiome research, yet achieving high species-level accuracy remains challenging for complex communities that span bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea, and these limitations are exacerbated in low-biomass, host-dominated samples. We introduce Metax, a cross-domain taxonomic profiler that integrates coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to distinguish true microbial signals from artifacts. Across >600 samples from host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, including benc
papers.summary: Metax is a new computational tool for taxonomic profiling of metagenomes that works across all domains of life (bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, archaea) with high species-level accuracy. It combines coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to separate genuine microbial signals from artifacts, and was validated on over 600 samples from diverse environments including low-biomass clinical samples.

papers.title: Phylogenomics of Desulfuromonadia supports reclassification of Geobacter psychrophilus as Irobacter psychrophilus comb. nov. and proposal of Geosyntrophus gen. nov.
papers.abstract: Genome-resolved phylogenomics reveals widespread misclassification of metal-reducing bacteria historically assigned to Geobacter based on 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, and highlights species that persist only as 16S rRNA entries without genomes for robust taxonomic resolution. Here, we resolve two such lineages by integrating whole-genome phylogeny with average amino acid identity (AAI) and percentage of conserved proteins (POCP) across 418 dereplicated genomes of Desulfuromonadia. We report a draft genome of the psychrophilic iron-reducing bacterium Geobacter psychrophilus (100% completeness). Phy
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved phylogenomics across 418 genomes of Desulfuromonadia to show that many metal-reducing bacteria historically classified as Geobacter based on 16S rRNA are misclassified. The authors reclassify Geobacter psychrophilus as Irobacter psychrophilus comb. nov. and propose the new genus Geosyntrophus, integrating whole-genome phylogeny with AAI and POCP metrics.

papers.title: Performance Profiles of Short DNA Barcode Segments for Family Level Detection of Asteraceae Within Asterales.
papers.abstract: Short DNA barcodes may facilitate sequence recovery from degraded material, but their ability to retain target-family identity while excluding related taxa varies among genomic regions. We computationally evaluated 16 nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial marker regions from 11 Asterales families using 279,956 NCBI locus-record matches and an accession-disjoint discovery/test design. Thirty-one candidate segments of 50-200 bp (mean, 98.55 bp) were screened in discovery data and evaluated for within-Asteraceae sequence recall, differentiation from non-Asteraceae Asterales, in silico primer behavi
papers.summary: This study computationally evaluated 16 nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial marker regions to identify short DNA barcode segments (50-200 bp) that can reliably identify the plant family Asteraceae while excluding related families within Asterales. Using nearly 280,000 NCBI locus records and a discovery/test design, they screened 31 candidate segments for within-family recall, differentiation from non-Asteraceae taxa, and primer behavior. The work provides a systematic performance profile of short barcodes for degraded-material applications at the family level.

papers.title: Spatially Specialized Nasopharynx-Rectal Microbiomes in Golden Snub-Nosed Monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana).
papers.abstract: Understanding the nasopharyngeal (NAS) and rectal (INT) microbiomes is critical to maintain host health. However, their functional roles in shaping microbial network structure and niche differentiation remain unexplored in most animal species, especially endangered primates. Here, we compared the NAS and INT microbiomes of golden snub-nosed monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana) using full-length 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and metagenomics, focusing on taxonomic composition, functional profiles (KEGG, CAZy, PHI), and microbial co-occurrence networks.
papers.summary: This study compared the nasopharyngeal and rectal microbiomes of endangered golden snub-nosed monkeys using full-length 16S rRNA sequencing and metagenomics, examining taxonomic composition, functional profiles, and microbial co-occurrence networks. The authors found that these two body sites harbor spatially specialized microbial communities with distinct functional capacities and network structures, highlighting niche differentiation in primate microbiomes.

papers.title: Effects of Dietary Glucose, Fructose, and Monosaccharide-to-Lard Energy Ratios on Cecal Microbiota Composition and Ecological Organization in Rats.
papers.abstract: Background: Although dietary fat and carbohydrates are major determinants of gut microbiota composition, their interactive effects across changing dietary monosaccharide-to-lard energy ratios remain incompletely understood. This study descriptively examined treatment-level cecal microbiome profiles across dietary gradients in which lard (L) was progressively replaced with glucose (G) or fructose (F). Methods: A carbohydrate-free, lard-rich control diet was formulated, and lard was progressively replaced with glucose or fructose while maintaining a constant protein-to-energy ratio. Cecal conten
papers.summary: This study examined how progressively replacing dietary lard with glucose or fructose affects the composition and ecological organization of the cecal microbiome in rats. The authors found that the type of monosaccharide and the ratio of monosaccharide-to-fat energy shape distinct microbial community profiles, with glucose and fructose producing different effects on community structure.

papers.title: Redundancy maintains microbial ecosystem functional potential despite taxonomic shifts between serpentine and nonserpentine soils.
papers.abstract: Environmental filtering and buffering are complementary processes responsible for stabilizing ecosystem services across landscapes. The extent to which either of these processes structures microbial composition and functions in extreme soil systems can be highly context-dependent, requiring site-specific examination to elucidate general principles of community function under stress. Serpentine soils have high amounts of heavy metals and magnesium and low levels of plant nutrients and exist in close proximity to nutrient-rich and plant-productive nonserpentine soils, making them an ideal system
papers.summary: This study examines microbial communities in serpentine soils, which are extreme environments with high heavy metals and low nutrients, compared to nearby nonserpentine soils. It finds that despite significant taxonomic shifts in microbial composition between the two soil types, the overall functional potential of the ecosystem remains stable, likely due to functional redundancy among different microbial taxa. This suggests that ecosystem services can be maintained even when species composition changes under environmental stress.

papers.title: New Insights into the Composition of the Early-Life Gut Microbiome: A Metagenomic Analysis of Fecal Samples in Children Up to 18 Months of Age.
papers.abstract: To determine the gut microbiome composition and associated factors in infants.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the gut microbiome composition in children up to 18 months of age, examining how it changes over this early developmental window. It also identifies factors associated with differences in microbiome composition among infants.

papers.title: Nanopore metagenomic sequencing links clinically relevant resistance determinants to pathogens.
papers.abstract: Culture-independent metagenomics enables the detection of plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes directly from clinical samples; however, the clinical significance of these genes depends on their bacterial host and genomic context, which metagenomics cannot fully infer. Nanopore sequencing technology intrinsically encodes epigenetic modifications such as methylation, which can be leveraged for plasmid-host associations from metagenomic data. Existing methods rely on the recovery of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), which can introduce bias towards abundant taxa and leave clini
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomic sequencing, which captures DNA methylation signals, to link plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes directly to their bacterial hosts in clinical samples without culturing. This approach overcomes the bias of existing MAG-based methods that favor abundant taxa, allowing clinically relevant resistance determinants to be assigned to specific pathogens.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys the rapidly expanding landscape of bacteriophage bioinformatics, cataloguing over 80 dedicated tools—most published since 2020—that cover tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology (limited by database completeness), machine learning (limited by labelled training data), and emerging approaches. The paper is aimed at experienced practitioners and developers seeking a structured overview of available methods and their constraints.

papers.title: Foundation Models for Microbiome Research: From Sequence Semantics to Community Dynamics and Multimodal World Models.
papers.abstract: Microbiome sequencing has advanced faster than microbiome understanding. Although large-scale 16S, metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and proteomic datasets have accumulated rapidly, most analyses remain cohort-specific and association-driven, limiting mechanistic insight, cross-study transferability, and robustness to technical confounding. Foundation models offer a new computational framework by learning reusable biological representations from large unlabeled datasets. In this Review, we present microbiome foundation models as a hierarchy spanning biological scales. Sequence-centric models ca
papers.summary: This review proposes a hierarchical framework for microbiome foundation models, spanning from sequence-level representations to community dynamics and multimodal 'world models.' It argues that these reusable, self-supervised representations can overcome the cohort-specific, association-driven limitations of current microbiome analyses and improve cross-study transferability.

papers.title: A retrospective metagenomic analysis of fecal microbiota transplantation donors from five countries: Safety considerations for donor screening and core microbiome profiles of qualified donors.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has been successfully applied on clinical aspects, but its clinical outcomes remain unpredictable due to inconsistent donor screening protocols across hospitals, institutions, and countries. Hence, a retrospective analysis of metagenomic data from published studies on FMT donors via a unified bioinformatics workflow might contribute to the understanding of the safety considerations for donor screening and the fecal microbial profiles of qualified donors. In this study, we reanalyzed metagenomic data of 475 screened donor fecal samples from 24 studies span
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed metagenomic data from 475 screened fecal donor samples across 24 studies spanning five countries using a unified bioinformatics workflow. The authors aimed to identify safety considerations for donor screening and characterize the core microbiome profiles of qualified FMT donors. The work highlights inconsistencies in donor screening protocols and proposes common microbial features that could inform standardized donor qualification criteria.

papers.title: Differential analysis of microbial interaction networks.
papers.abstract: Microbiome studies increasingly indicate that disease-associated shifts cannot be understood from compositional changes alone. The functional architecture of microbial communities-encoded in patterns of association among microbial gene families-may reveal how these systems reorganize across biological conditions. Here, we present a network-based framework for characterizing microbiome rewiring across conditions. The approach combines condition-specific network inference, differential network analysis, and pathway-level network analysis to identify associations that are gained, lost, or altered
papers.summary: The paper introduces a network-based framework for analyzing how microbial interaction networks change across biological conditions, rather than just looking at shifts in microbial composition. It combines condition-specific network inference, differential network analysis, and pathway-level analysis to identify microbial associations that are gained, lost, or altered between conditions.

papers.title: The Gut Microbiota in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Evaluation of Microbial Profiles, Disease Activity, Biomarkers, and Treatment Response.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with complex etiopathogenesis, and variable clinical course. The human gastrointestinal (GI) tract is a dynamic ecosystem in which micro-organisms influence metabolism, immune signalling, and pathogen resistance. Understanding these interactions is key to exploring the microbiota's role in RA. This review examines how intestinal and oral microbiota differ in RA patients and influence disease activity and treatment response.
papers.summary: This review examines how intestinal and oral microbial communities differ in rheumatoid arthritis patients compared to healthy individuals, and how these differences relate to disease activity and treatment response. It synthesizes evidence on the gut microbiome's role in immune signaling and RA pathogenesis, highlighting the potential for microbiota-based biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: SimpleMicrobiome: An integrated web-based platform for streamlined microbiome data analysis and visualization.
papers.abstract: Microbiome studies require multiple analytical steps after initial sequence processing. These steps commonly include data harmonization, preprocessing, taxonomic profiling, diversity analysis, differential abundance testing, predictive modeling, network inference, and preparation of publication-ready outputs. Although robust packages are available for many of these tasks, routine use often depends on command-line workflows, repeated data reformatting, and method-specific scripting. These requirements can limit accessibility for experimental researchers and complicate consistent analysis across
papers.summary: SimpleMicrobiome is a new web-based platform that integrates multiple microbiome analysis steps—including data harmonization, taxonomic profiling, diversity analysis, differential abundance testing, predictive modeling, and network inference—into a single user-friendly interface. It aims to make routine microbiome analyses more accessible to experimental researchers by reducing reliance on command-line workflows and method-specific scripting.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Multidimensional Phenotyping of Gut Metabolic States for Personalized Prebiotic, Probiotic, and Postbiotic Strategies.
papers.abstract: This study presents multidimensional physicochemical phenotyping of human gut metabolic states using integrated multimodal profiling and machine learning. A total of 680 stool samples were analyzed using time-resolved optical, electrochemical, acoustic, magnetic, and spectral measurements implemented in a compact 3D-printed screening platform. Multivariate analysis explained 78.4% of structured variance, and cluster optimization identified seven primary clusters and 26 structurally retained subclusters representing proteolytic, saccharolytic, bile/lipid-rich, oxidative, diarrheal, pigment-link
papers.summary: This study used a compact 3D-printed platform combining optical, electrochemical, acoustic, magnetic, and spectral measurements with machine learning to profile 680 human stool samples. Multivariate analysis captured 78.4% of structured variance and identified seven primary gut metabolic clusters (e.g., proteolytic, saccharolytic, bile/lipid-rich) with 26 subclusters. The approach aims to enable personalized prebiotic, probiotic, and postbiotic strategies based on individual gut metabolic states.

papers.title: Inclusion of Multi-Omic Biomarkers Improves Prediction Accuracy of Response, Relapse, and Overall Survival in Acute Myeloid Leukemia Patients Receiving High-Intensity Induction Chemotherapy.
papers.abstract: Despite advancements in genetic markers for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) risk stratification, outcome prediction remains challenging due to disease heterogeneity and dynamic genetic changes, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers to improve AML treatment strategies and patient outcomes. To refine outcome predictions, we investigated the use of microbial-derived biomarkers to predict composite complete remission (CRc), relapse, and survival for patients on high- and low-intensity regimens, and to integrate those variables into the widely clinically utilized European Leukemia Network (ELN
papers.summary: This study investigated whether microbial-derived biomarkers, combined with multi-omic data, can improve prediction of complete remission, relapse, and overall survival in acute myeloid leukemia patients receiving high-intensity induction chemotherapy. The authors found that incorporating these multi-omic biomarkers into existing risk models like the European Leukemia Network classification improved prediction accuracy. The work suggests that microbial-derived features may serve as useful complementary biomarkers for AML outcome stratification.

papers.title: Evaluating the probiotic potential of Bacillus pumilus HFS2 isolated from the gut microbiota of Heteropneustes fossilis for aquaculture applications.
papers.abstract: Probiotics are increasingly used in aquaculture to enhance fish survival, growth, and health, offering a sustainable approach to fish farming.
papers.summary: This study isolated Bacillus pumilus HFS2 from the gut microbiota of the freshwater catfish Heteropneustes fossilis and evaluated its potential as a probiotic for aquaculture. The authors characterize the strain's beneficial properties, suggesting it could serve as a sustainable alternative to antibiotics in fish farming.

papers.title: Integrated immunoinformatics for the design of novel multi-epitope vaccine and identification of new drug targets against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, a multidrug-resistant superbug.
papers.abstract: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is a multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen causing severe hospital-acquired infections, especially in immunocompromised patients. The absence of an effective vaccine and rising antibiotic resistance underscore the need for novel interventions. This study employed an integrated reverse vaccinology and computational analyses to identify new immunogenic targets, design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV), and propose potential drug targets.
papers.summary: This study applies reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics to the multidrug-resistant pathogen Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, identifying immunogenic protein targets and designing a multi-epitope vaccine construct in silico. It also proposes potential new drug targets to complement the vaccine approach against this hospital-acquired superbug.

papers.title: In silico genome mining and characterization of putative horse feces-derived bacterial phytases as potential monogastric animal feed additive candidates.
papers.abstract: Phytic acid exerts a significant antinutritional effect in poultry, swine, and fish, which can be mitigated by supplementing monogastric feeds with efficient microbial phytases. Accordingly, mining bacterial genomes for novel phytases represents a strategic computational approach to identifying candidates for improving monogastric animal nutrition. In this study, 162 bacterial genomes associated with horse feces were systematically mined using an in silico pipeline to identify and characterize putative phytases.A total of 69 non-redundant sequences were identified and classified as histidine a
papers.summary: This study used computational genome mining to search 162 bacterial genomes from horse feces for novel phytase enzymes, identifying 69 non-redundant candidate sequences. These putative phytases are proposed as potential feed additives to help monogastric animals like poultry and swine better digest phytic acid, an antinutritional compound in their feed.

papers.title: Antimicrobial resistance as a signature of soil restoration across a 143-year chronosequence.
papers.abstract: Restoring agriculturally degraded habitats to species-rich grasslands is a vital conservation objective. During restoration, how the soil resistome matures alongside microbial community composition and function remains unclear. Here, we tested two competing hypotheses: whether the soil resistome co-occurs through a microbial structural maturation, in which soil restoration is associated with higher-order biotic interactions, or whether antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is instead associated with the competitive pressures and high bacterial taxonomic richness found in disturbed, eutrophic arable l
papers.summary: This study tracked soil antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes across a 143-year grassland restoration chronosequence to test whether the resistome matures alongside microbial community structure or instead reflects competitive pressures in disturbed agricultural soils. The authors found that AMR signatures are linked to soil restoration status, suggesting the resistome can serve as an indicator of restoration progress. The work clarifies how resistance genes change as degraded arable land recovers into species-rich grassland.

papers.title: The cervicovaginal gut microbiota axis as a key determinant of systemic physiology.
papers.abstract: The gut and vaginal microbiomes are both essential to human health, yet they have largely been studied in isolation. Gut microbiota are central to host metabolism, immunity, and the gut-brain axis, while the vaginal microbiome, typically dominated by Lactobacillus species, protects against infection and shapes reproductive outcomes. Although dysbiosis at either site has been linked to systemic disease, the possibility that these communities are interrelated and that the vaginal microbiome could serve as a clinically accessible proxy for systemic microbial states remains underexplored. This rep
papers.summary: This review argues that the gut and vaginal microbiomes should be studied as an interconnected 'cervicovaginal-gut microbiota axis' rather than in isolation, since dysbiosis at either site is linked to systemic disease. The authors propose that the vaginal microbiome, being more clinically accessible, could serve as a proxy for systemic microbial states and host physiology.

papers.title: A gavage-fomite based method to generate mouse models with natural microbiota.
papers.abstract: Laboratory-raised specific pathogen-free (SPF) mice have been indispensable for fundamental immunology research, yet their reliability in predicting human clinical outcomes has been questionable. A major factor contributing to this disconnect is the sanitized housing environment, which deprives laboratory mice of physiological microbial exposure critical for immune maturation. Various approaches have been developed to introduce microbes to SPF mice, aiming to mimic human-like microbial experiences and engender adult human-like immune traits. However, some of these methods, specifically the pet
papers.summary: The paper presents a gavage-fomite based method for transferring natural microbiota to laboratory mice, aiming to better mimic human microbial exposure and immune maturation. This approach addresses the limitations of specific pathogen-free (SPF) mice, whose sanitized environment may reduce their reliability for predicting human clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Dataset characterising dominant bacterial phylotypes across animal manure-enriched composting microcosms for crude oil waste sludge bioremediation.
papers.abstract: The dataset provides a complete record of microbial, functional, physicochemical, and contaminant dynamics from controlled co-composting microcosms designed to remediate petroleum refinery sludge using targeted animal manure amendments. Five treatments-cow, pig, horse, and poultry manures, as well as an unamended control-were monitored over 300 days. The study incorporated amplicon-based 16S rRNA gene sequencing, functional gene inference, culture-based validation, bulk chemistry, and chromatographic analyses. Illumina MiSeq profiling of the V1-V3 regions identified 359 bacterial genera (raw O
papers.summary: This dataset tracks microbial community composition, functional gene profiles, physicochemical properties, and contaminant degradation across five composting microcosms (cow, pig, horse, poultry manure, and unamended control) used to bioremediate petroleum refinery sludge over 300 days. It combines 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, functional gene inference, culture-based validation, and chromatographic chemistry to identify dominant bacterial phylotypes driving hydrocarbon breakdown. The resource is intended to support comparative and meta-analyses of manure-amended bioremediation strategies.

papers.title: Bronchoalveolar Lavage Microbiota in Critically Ill Patients with Aspiration Pneumonia: An Exploratory Comparison with Community-Acquired Pneumonia and Analysis of Gemella Detection and Mortality.
papers.abstract: Aspiration pneumonia (AP) is a common and severe infection among critically ill older adults, but its lower respiratory tract microbiota and clinical associations remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory study characterizes the bronchoalveolar lavage microbiota of critically ill patients with aspiration pneumonia and compares it to community-acquired pneumonia, with a specific focus on Gemella detection and its relationship to mortality. The findings suggest distinct microbial signatures in aspiration pneumonia that may have prognostic implications, though the exploratory design limits definitive conclusions.

papers.title: Gut microbiome-metabolome signatures of osteosarcopenia in fracture patients in China.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcopenia, defined as the coexistence of low bone mass and sarcopenia, is a disabling musculoskeletal condition, yet its gut microbial and metabolic characteristics in clinical populations remain incompletely understood. Integrative multi-omics approaches may help clarify species-metabolite networks associated with this condition, particularly in fracture patients.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics to characterize gut microbiome and metabolome signatures in Chinese fracture patients with osteosarcopenia, a condition combining low bone mass and muscle loss. It aims to identify species-metabolite networks associated with the disease, addressing a gap in clinical understanding of the gut-muscle-bone axis.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of the fecal microbiome in Lamp2 knockout mice reveals limited genotype-associated differences under standard housing.
papers.abstract: Lysosomal pathways influence host-microbe interactions, but the microbiome consequences of lysosomal dysfunction remain incompletely defined. LAMP2 is required for autophagosome-lysosome fusion, and pathogenic variants in LAMP2 cause Danon disease. Whether Lamp2 loss alters the gut microbiome in vivo has not been systematically evaluated using methods that profile both taxonomic composition and microbial functional potential, such as shotgun metagenomics.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the fecal microbiome of Lamp2 knockout mice, a model for Danon disease, compared to wild-type mice under standard housing conditions. Despite the known role of lysosomal pathways in host-microbe interactions, the analysis found only limited taxonomic and functional differences associated with the Lamp2 genotype. The results suggest that Lamp2 loss alone does not substantially reshape the gut microbiome in this controlled setting.

papers.title: Genome-resolved gut metagenomics identifies an Escherichia coli-Collinsella signature associated with Wagner 4 gangrenous diabetic foot ulcers.
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are a major complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus, but whether the gut microbiome captures systemic microbial features associated with advanced ulcer severity remains unclear. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 43 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and active DFU, comparing Wagner grades 1-3 (n = 30) with Wagner 4 gangrenous disease (n = 13). De novo assembly and binning recovered 440 dereplicated metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) meeting medium-quality or high-completeness/low-contamination thresholds. Community-level diversit
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 43 type 2 diabetes patients with diabetic foot ulcers to compare gut microbiome features between Wagner grades 1-3 and Wagner 4 gangrenous disease. They recovered 440 metagenome-assembled genomes and identified an Escherichia coli-Collinsella signature associated with the more severe Wagner 4 gangrenous ulcers. The findings suggest that gut microbiome composition may reflect or contribute to systemic features linked to advanced ulcer severity.

papers.title: A metagenomic analysis of the gut microbiota in a mouse model of fish allergy.
papers.abstract: Fish are among the most frequent causes of immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated food allergies (Type I). Currently, there is no known cure for fish allergy and individuals who are sensitized have to practice strict, lifelong avoidance of fish products in their diets. The relationship between gut microbiome and food allergies is currently a major topic of discussion; these pathologies involve the development of dysbiosis, which is a microbial imbalance resulting from immune-related mechanisms. Recent studies have provided evidence that individuals suffering from food allergies, display an intestinal
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize gut microbiota composition in a mouse model of fish allergy, aiming to identify microbial taxa or functional pathways associated with allergic sensitization. The work contributes to the growing body of evidence linking gut dysbiosis to IgE-mediated food allergy development.

papers.title: Beyond the Pancreas: The Gut Microbiota in Acute Pancreatitis - From Mechanisms to Therapeutic Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Acute pancreatitis is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease in which severe forms are frequently complicated by intestinal barrier failure, dysbiosis, bacterial translocation, infected necrosis, systemic inflammation, and organ dysfunction. Growing clinical and experimental evidence suggests that the gut microbiota may contribute to disease progression and represents a potential, although incompletely validated, therapeutic target. Importantly, acute pancreatitis-associated dysbiosis involves not only taxonomic shifts but also functional metabolic reprogramming, including reduced short-chain fa
papers.summary: This review examines how gut microbiota contribute to acute pancreatitis progression, focusing on dysbiosis, intestinal barrier failure, and bacterial translocation that can lead to infected necrosis and organ dysfunction. It highlights that the dysbiosis involves not just taxonomic shifts but also functional metabolic changes such as reduced short-chain fatty acid production, positioning the microbiota as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: The chromosomal genome sequence of a staghorn coral, Acropora cf.  manni (Scleractinia: Acroporidae).
papers.abstract: We present a genome assembly from a colony sample of Acropora cf. manni (staghorn coral; Cnidaria; Anthozoa; Scleractinia; Acroporidae). The assembly contains two haplotypes with total lengths of 459.26 megabases and 489.30 megabases. Most of haplotype 1 (94.39%) is scaffolded into 14 chromosomal pseudomolecules. Haplotype 2 was assembled to scaffold level. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled, with a length of 18.48 kilobases. Metagenome binning recovered one bacterial bin from the phylum Chlamydiota.
papers.summary: This paper reports a chromosome-level genome assembly for a staghorn coral, Acropora cf. manni, with two haplotypes (459 Mb and 489 Mb) and 14 chromosomal pseudomolecules for haplotype 1. It also includes the mitochondrial genome and a recovered bacterial symbiont bin from the phylum Chlamydiota. The resource provides a foundation for coral genomics and reef conservation research.

papers.title: Gut microbiota dynamics and metabolic pathways associated with bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis progression.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive respiratory disease characterized by epithelial injury, aberrant repair and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. Although the gut-lung axis is increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders, stage-resolved characterization of gut microbiota taxonomic and functional potential during PF development is limited.
papers.summary: This study characterizes how gut microbiota composition and predicted metabolic functions change across stages of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in a mouse model. It provides stage-resolved taxonomic and functional profiles that link gut microbial shifts to fibrosis progression via the gut-lung axis.

papers.title: Short-read genome skimming enables molecular barcoding of old myxomycete collections.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Illumina-based genome skimming for barcoding myxomycete herbarium collections ranging from 29 to 91 years in age. We successfully retrieved partial sequences of the standard marker gene (nucSSU) in all cases, as well as additional markers (mtSSU, EF1a, and COI) for certain collections. Altogether, 28 genes were recognized in the studied material. In a 33-year-old specimen of Lindbladia tubulina, the assembly reached an N50 of 4.19 kb, enabling the recovery of extended functional loci. The input genomic DNA quantity emerges as the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that Illumina genome skimming can successfully recover barcode sequences from myxomycete herbarium specimens up to 91 years old, retrieving the standard nucSSU marker in all cases and additional markers in some. The amount of input genomic DNA was the primary factor determining success, and one 33-year-old specimen yielded an assembly with N50 of 4.19 kb, enabling recovery of extended functional loci.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors in sediments of river Yamuna.
papers.abstract: Riverine sediments serve as critical reservoirs of microbial diversity and functional genes, reflecting both natural ecological processes and anthropogenic impacts. In the present study, we employed a shotgun metagenomic approach to investigate microbial community composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, and virulence factors in sediments collected from three environmentally distinct locations of the Yamuna River near Agra, India, representing BSA, TGY, and YEA. The sediment DNA was subjected to high-throughput Illumina sequencing, followed by quality control, assembly, and open read
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile microbial communities, antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence factors in sediments from three sites along the Yamuna River near Agra, India. The findings reveal how anthropogenic pollution shapes the resistome and virulome in riverine sediments, highlighting sediments as reservoirs for clinically relevant AMR and virulence determinants.

papers.title: Multi-dimensional dynamic assessment revealed the antibiotic-induced pseudo-germ-free model in SD rats stabilized within 4 days.
papers.abstract: Pseudo-germ-free (PGF) animal models are typically established after 7 days of antibiotic treatment, mostly validated using 16S rRNA sequencing. However, this method cannot distinguish live from dead bacteria and may overestimate the required depletion time. We investigated whether PGF model establishment in Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats could be completed in shorter than 7 days using an antibiotic cocktail. Gut microbiota was dynamically monitored with antibiotic cocktail treatment on days 0 to 7 by aerobic/anaerobic bacterial culture, Gram staining, and 16S rRNA sequencing, alongside body weight,
papers.summary: This study shows that a pseudo-germ-free (PGF) gut model in Sprague-Dawley rats can be established in just 4 days of antibiotic cocktail treatment, rather than the standard 7 days. By combining aerobic/anaerobic culture, Gram staining, and 16S rRNA sequencing, the authors demonstrate that culture-based methods reveal faster bacterial depletion than sequencing alone, which cannot distinguish live from dead bacteria.

papers.title: Oral microbiome and lesion-associated microbiological findings in medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: a systematic review and evidence map.
papers.abstract: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) may involve microbial colonization, anaerobic organisms, and biofilm formation, but whether it has a reproducible microbial signature remains unclear. We mapped the human microbiological evidence in MRONJ.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This systematic review and evidence map synthesizes human microbiological studies of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), examining whether the condition has a reproducible microbial signature involving anaerobic organisms and biofilm formation. The authors map the existing evidence to identify consistent oral microbiome and lesion-associated findings and highlight gaps in the literature.

papers.title: Prenatal valproic acid exposure in rodent models of autism: a systematic review of neurobehavioral physiological alterations.
papers.abstract: Rodent models based on prenatal valproic acid (VPA) exposure are widely used to investigate autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related neurobehavioral and biological alterations. Over the past two years, the rapid expansion of VPA-based research incorporating advanced molecular, neuroimaging, electrophysiological, and microbiota analyses has generated a substantial but fragmented body of evidence.
papers.summary: This systematic review consolidates evidence from rodent models of prenatal valproic acid exposure, a widely used paradigm for studying autism spectrum disorder. It synthesizes recent findings across neurobehavioral, molecular, neuroimaging, electrophysiological, and microbiota domains to address the fragmented state of the literature.

papers.title: LMDmapper: an open-source desktop tool for spatial mapping of laser microdissection samples.
papers.abstract: Laser microdissection (LMD) enables researchers to isolate targeted microsamples from microscopy slide specimens for downstream molecular analyses. While traditionally employed for isolating eukaryotic cells from complex tissues, LMD is starting to be used for micro-scale spatial microbiome analyses, which require the precise location of the microsamples to be tracked for downstream spatial analyses. To address this need, we present LMDmapper, an open-source desktop application that allows designing, tracking and logging micron-scale spatial microsample data and metadata from LMD sessions. The
papers.summary: LMDmapper is an open-source desktop application that helps researchers design, track, and log micron-scale spatial data from laser microdissection sessions. It addresses the emerging need for precise location tracking when LMD is used for spatial microbiome analyses, where microsample positions must be recorded for downstream spatial interpretation.

papers.title: Targeting cancer hallmarks with microbiome-derived bacteriocins and postbiotics: molecular mechanisms and translational opportunities in oncology.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome is an abundant reservoir of bioactive molecules with considerable therapeutic potential in oncology. Among these microbial products, bacteriocins and other postbiotic metabolites have emerged as promising anticancer agents due to their diverse biological activities and ability to modulate multiple cancer-related pathways. Growing evidence suggests that microbiome-derived compounds may provide novel opportunities for the development of safer and more targeted cancer therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review examines how bacteriocins and other postbiotic metabolites produced by the human microbiome can target multiple cancer hallmarks, positioning them as potential anticancer agents. It discusses the molecular mechanisms by which these microbial compounds modulate cancer-related pathways and outlines translational opportunities for developing safer, more targeted cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Sishen wan modulates gut microbial and short-chain fatty-acid imbalances and ameliorates behavioral and inflammatory abnormalities in mice with chronic sleep deprivation.
papers.abstract: Chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) disrupts mood-related behavior, gut microbial ecology, and inflammatory homeostasis. Sishen Wan (SSW), a medicinal plant formula used clinically for chronic diarrhea, has shown microbiota- and inflammation-modulating effects in colitis models, but its protective effects under sleep-deprivation conditions remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether Sishen Wan (SSW), a traditional medicinal plant formula, can counteract the negative effects of chronic sleep deprivation in mice. The authors find that SSW treatment rebalances gut microbial communities and short-chain fatty acid levels, and improves behavioral and inflammatory abnormalities caused by sleep deprivation.

papers.title: The circulating metatranscriptome in acute myeloid leukemia patients: an RNA-seq reanalysis.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome comprises the collection of microbiota residing on or within human tissues. It is now well-established that microbial composition impacts an individual's health. In the cancer realm, the vast majority of microbiome studies have been focused either on the gut, or at the site of solid tumors. Few studies have assessed microbial content at the site of hematological malignancies - blood and bone marrow. Here we characterize the circulating metatranscriptome (i.e. the bacterial and viral RNA in circulation) of 411 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). We find that the cir
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed RNA-seq data from 411 acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients to characterize the circulating metatranscriptome—bacterial and viral RNA present in blood. It represents one of the few efforts to profile microbial content in hematological malignancies, moving beyond the gut and solid tumor focus of most cancer microbiome research. The abstract is truncated, so specific microbial signatures or clinical associations are not fully described.

papers.title: Age-specific alterations in gut microbiota-plasma metabolome networks in first-episode, drug-naïve major depressive disorder: adolescent versus adult patients.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibits pronounced age-related pathophysiological heterogeneity, yet the distinct signatures of the microbiota-gut-brain (MGB) axis between adolescent and adult patients remain inadequately characterized. This study aimed to elucidate age-specific MGB axis dysregulation by integrating gut microbiota profiling, plasma metabolomics, and their interactive networks in first-episode, drug-naïve MDD patients across these two developmental stages.
papers.summary: This study compares gut microbiota and plasma metabolome profiles, along with their interaction networks, between first-episode, drug-naïve adolescent and adult patients with major depressive disorder. It aims to identify age-specific dysregulation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis, suggesting that MDD pathophysiology differs between developmental stages.

papers.title: Sampling method influences hemolymph bacterial communities in the eastern oyster, Crassostrea virginica.
papers.abstract: As the microbiome becomes increasingly recognized for its role in driving animal health and disease, accurate characterization of microbial community composition is essential. With this research comes the critical need for standardized sampling methods along with an understanding of the biases inherent to these methods. In oysters, hemolymph is a valuable system for microbiome research due to its diverse physiological functions, role as an indicator of health, and ease of collection. Unfortunately, much of the current literature regarding oyster hemolymph microbiome composition is opaque in it
papers.summary: This study examines how different sampling methods affect the bacterial communities detected in eastern oyster hemolymph. The authors find that sampling approach introduces significant biases in microbiome composition, highlighting the need for standardized protocols in oyster microbiome research.

papers.title: Microbiome-metabolome interaction reveals rhizosphere ecological, bioactive, and antioxidant responses of Paeonia lactiflora Pall. to intercropping and harvest timing.
papers.abstract: Paeonia lactiflora Pall. (P. lactiflora) is a medicinal plant with considerable economic value. During its growth, root secondary metabolism and rhizosphere microbes interact closely; however, no systematic study has examined microbiome and metabolome dynamics under different planting systems and harvest times. To address this, we employed amplicon sequencing for microbial diversity and untargeted metabolomics for metabolite profiling. The datasets were then integrated, and correlation analysis was performed. We measured paeoniflorin by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), total phen
papers.summary: This study integrated rhizosphere microbiome profiling (amplicon sequencing) with untargeted metabolomics to examine how intercropping systems and harvest timing affect Paeonia lactiflora, a valuable medicinal plant. The authors identified correlations between microbial community composition and secondary metabolite profiles, including the bioactive compound paeoniflorin, revealing ecological and antioxidant responses linked to cultivation practices. The findings suggest that intercropping and harvest timing can be optimized to enhance medicinal quality through microbiome-metabolome interactions.

papers.title: The effectiveness of the intervention model based on cognitive behavioral therapy in reducing risky sexual behaviors among MSM.
papers.abstract: Based on CBT theory and the Internet, we established an intervention model targeting high-risk sexual behavior patterns in MSM. We then conducted a randomized controlled trial (n = 50) to assess the impact of the CBT-based intervention on high-risk sexual behaviors and gut microbiota changes in this population.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial tested an internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy intervention designed to reduce risky sexual behaviors among men who have sex with men (MSM). The study also examined changes in gut microbiota alongside behavioral outcomes in the 50 participants.

papers.title: Social and biological pathways linking relationships with companion animals to human well-being.
papers.abstract: Companion animals are widely recognized for their potential to support human mental health and well-being. These benefits may arise through changes in social relationships and physiological processes. This study examined whether dog and cat ownership and attachment promote closer social relationships and higher well-being, the relative magnitude of direct and indirect effects of companion animals on well-being, and whether physiological factors, including cortisol concentration and gut microbiota composition, are involved in these processes.
papers.summary: This study investigates how dog and cat ownership and attachment relate to human well-being, testing both social pathways (closer relationships) and biological pathways (cortisol and gut microbiota composition). It aims to quantify the relative strength of direct versus indirect effects of companion animals on well-being.

papers.title: Anaerobic stress index to predict microbial ecological shifts in clear aligners.
papers.abstract: Clear aligners are clinically perceived as periodontally 'friendlier' than fixed appliances (FA), yet localized gingivitis persists. Salivary diagnostics often mask site-specific dysbiosis through a 'dilution effect'. This study aimed to characterize distinct ecological pressures and propose a novel anaerobic stress index (ASI) to quantify localized microbial burden.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the distinct ecological pressures on oral microbial communities in patients wearing clear aligners versus fixed orthodontic appliances, arguing that saliva-based diagnostics dilute site-specific dysbiosis. The authors propose a novel anaerobic stress index (ASI) to quantify localized microbial burden and predict ecological shifts.

papers.title: Current Concepts in Periprosthetic Joint Infection: Modern Biomarkers, Microbiome Insights, Molecular Diagnostics, and Emerging Prevention Strategies.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the leading causes of revision arthroplasty and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Diagnosis remains challenging because of heterogeneous clinical presentations, the limited sensitivity of conventional inflammatory markers in chronic and low-grade infections, culture-negative cases, and biofilm-mediated pathogen persistence. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in the diagnosis and prevention of PJI, with a particular focus on synovial and serum biomarkers, microbiome-related susceptibility,
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes recent advances in diagnosing and preventing periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), a major complication of joint replacement surgery. It focuses on modern synovial and serum biomarkers, microbiome-related susceptibility factors, molecular diagnostics, and emerging prevention strategies to address the limitations of conventional culture and inflammatory markers.

papers.title: The association between neonatal respiratory distress syndrome and gut microbiota dysbiosis: evidence from metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) is a common and life-threatening respiratory disorder that affects newborns, significantly impacting their health and survival rates. In recent years, the potential role of the gut-lung axis in NRDS has garnered increasing attention; however, the specific mechanisms involved remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between NRDS and gut microbial composition and functional profiles using shotgun metagenomic sequencing.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare gut microbial composition and functional profiles in newborns with neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) versus controls. The findings provide evidence of gut microbiota dysbiosis associated with NRDS, supporting a potential role for the gut-lung axis in this condition.
